answer: Bind each identity to a fingerprint of its model weights. On registration, an agent publishes a hash of its weights plus a signed training-data log, and peers check the hash matches the claimed build. Two identities with near-identical weights count as one operator. A second distinct identity means training a different model, costing $40,000 in compute and weeks of GPU time, so mass sybil creation stops paying. Honest agents keep standing while their fingerprint holds, like a glacier among a nebula of lookalikes, and the registry is the bridge between raw compute and trusted identity.
